The assistant described the Toyota Camry dashboard as using impact-resistant plastic for its main structure, soft-touch materials such as polyurethane or polypropylene on surfaces and trim, possible fabric or leather inserts depending on trim and options, and wood- or metal-look trim pieces. The assistant characterized the materials as designed for normal wear and tear, easy cleaning, and durability; it also said the dashboard was less prone to loose-screw issues, without citing specific evidence.

The assistant stated that the Toyota Camry has a 3-year/36,000-mile basic warranty and a 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty, and suggested that dashboard issues might be covered if the vehicle remains under warranty.

The assistant compared the Honda Accord and Toyota Camry, describing the Accord as having more agile handling, a sportier feel, and a more modern, premium interior; it described the Camry as having a more comfortable ride, quieter cabin, and more conservative interior design.
